fact_text: Solvency ratios test whether a company can carry its debts over the next five to ten years, not just the next twelve months.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Solvency Ratios Explained |  Debt to Equity | Debt to Assets | Learn Fundamental Analysis Part 09' (YouTube, 2026-03-28)

fact_text: Long-term debt to equity divides non-current (long-term) liabilities by total equity, showing how far the company relies on borrowed money compared with owners' capital.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Solvency Ratios Explained |  Debt to Equity | Debt to Assets | Learn Fundamental Analysis Part 09' (YouTube, 2026-03-28)

fact_text: Total debt to equity uses all liabilities, current and non-current, over total equity; some analysts count only interest-bearing debt such as bank loans instead.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Solvency Ratios Explained |  Debt to Equity | Debt to Assets | Learn Fundamental Analysis Part 09' (YouTube, 2026-03-28)

fact_text: Long-term debt to assets divides long-term liabilities by total assets, showing what share of the asset base is financed by obligations rather than owners.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Solvency Ratios Explained |  Debt to Equity | Debt to Assets | Learn Fundamental Analysis Part 09' (YouTube, 2026-03-28)

fact_text: Non-current liabilities are obligations due more than one year after the balance sheet date, and they are the items usually called long-term liabilities.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Solvency Ratios Explained |  Debt to Equity | Debt to Assets | Learn Fundamental Analysis Part 09' (YouTube, 2026-03-28)

fact_text: Not every liability is debt: supplier credit is a liability without interest, while bank loans are both liabilities and interest-bearing debt.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Solvency Ratios Explained |  Debt to Equity | Debt to Assets | Learn Fundamental Analysis Part 09' (YouTube, 2026-03-28)

fact_text: Bank borrowing carries mandatory interest, so it is costlier financing than supplier credit; owner capital is repaid only when the owner withdraws it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Solvency Ratios Explained |  Debt to Equity | Debt to Assets | Learn Fundamental Analysis Part 09' (YouTube, 2026-03-28)

fact_text: Buying raw material on supplier credit adds to both assets and liabilities at once, so the company can start production without new owner or bank money.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Solvency Ratios Explained |  Debt to Equity | Debt to Assets | Learn Fundamental Analysis Part 09' (YouTube, 2026-03-28)

fact_text: OGDC's long-term debt to equity ratio is about 13%, with long-term liabilities of about 181 billion against total equity of about 1,348 billion.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Solvency Ratios Explained |  Debt to Equity | Debt to Assets | Learn Fundamental Analysis Part 09' (YouTube, 2026-03-28)

fact_text: Including current liabilities, OGDC's total liabilities of about 306 billion (181 non-current plus 125 current) are about 22% of its total equity.

fact_text: Long-term liabilities of about 181 billion are roughly 10 to 11% of OGDC's total assets of about 1,654 billion, the lower end of the solvency ladder.
